record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: For CSL over arbitrary metric models, determine the exact computational complexity of the satisfiability problem. Also determine what changes when CSL is extended with nominals, meaning singleton-valued location constants.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let CSL (the logic of comparative concept similarity) be the propositional modal language built from a countable set of propositional variables using Boolean connectives and a binary modal operator ⇋, where A ⇋ B is read as "closer to A than to B". A metric model is a triple M = (Δ, d, ν), where (Δ, d) is a metric space (Δ ≠ ∅ and d: Δ×Δ → ℝ≥0 satisfies d(x,y)=0 iff x=y, symmetry, and the triangle inequality) and ν assigns to each propositional variable a subset of Δ. The interpretation [[·]]^M extends ν by the usual Boolean clauses together with

  [[A ⇋ B]]^M = { x ∈ Δ : there exists y ∈ [[A]]^M such that for every z ∈ [[B]]^M, d(x,y) < d(x,z) }.

A formula φ is satisfiable over metric models if there is a metric model M and a point x ∈ Δ with x ∈ [[φ]]^M. The metric-satisfiability problem for CSL asks, given φ, whether such M and x exist.

(a) Determine the exact computational complexity of the satisfiability problem for CSL with respect to the class of all metric models.

(b) Let CSL+Nom denote the extension of CSL with nominals, i.e., a countable set of location constants {i, j, k, …}, where each nominal is required to be interpreted as a singleton subset of Δ. Determine the exact computational complexity of the satisfiability problem for CSL+Nom over the class of all metric models, and describe how (if at all) it differs from the complexity of plain CSL over metric models.
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature shows that CSL satisfiability is ExpTime-complete over arbitrary (symmetric) finite distance spaces, undecidable over ℝ, ℚ, ℤ and their finite subspaces (via reduction from Hilbert's 10th problem), and decidable in restricted cases (e.g. minspaces, triangular models). However, the exact complexity over the class of all metric models, and the impact of adding nominals to CSL in that setting, are listed as open problems and no published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Comparative Similarity, Tree Automata, and Diophantine Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Satisfiability is ExpTime-complete for all finite symmetric distance spaces; undecidable over finite subspaces of ℝ^n via Diophantine equations.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity is known for distance-space semantics and for Euclidean subspaces, but the metric case (and with nominals) is treated as open.

status_evidence.title: Preferential Semantics for the Logic of Comparative Similarity over Triangular and Metric Models
status_evidence.snippet: Provides preferential characterisations and tableaux for CSL over metric and triangular models, leaving tight complexity bounds as further work.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses metric CSL via preferential semantics but does not pin down tight complexity bounds, consistent with the problem being open.
